last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarter ever, but about half of the earnings jump came from volatile investment gains.

takeaways.label: Record, investment-aided profit
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS excluding one-time items rose 22% to a record $2.85. Variable investment income, which swings with markets, jumped 49% to $720 million.

takeaways.label: Broad growth
takeaways.text: Core revenue excluding big pension deals rose 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Europe/Middle East/Africa earnings rose 30% excluding one-time items. Group Benefits rose 14%.

takeaways.label: Weak spots
takeaways.text: Latin America earnings excluding one-time items fell 5% on a currency-neutral basis. Asia sales dropped 6%, and the expense ratio edged up to 11.9% from 11.6%.

takeaways.label: Book value split
takeaways.text: Reported book value per share fell 22% to $30.73, while adjusted book value rose 5% to $59.41. Adjusted return on equity was 19.6% excluding one-time items.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
